Title: Stocks tumble as AI panic sweeps markets, bonds draw haven demand
Author: By Ankur Banerjee and Tom Westbrook   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 7:53 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T06:53:10+00:00
=== BODY ===
SINGAPORE, Nov 6 (Reuters) - A steep rout in technology stocks on Friday rippled through markets on fears that the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections would increase regulatory scrutiny of AI and slow the data centre build-out, sending investors to the safety of bonds.
Japan's Nikkei slumped 6%, its deepest one-day drop since April ‌2025. Benchmark share price indices in South Korea and Taiwan similarly plunged more than 8% after the opening bell, before cutting losses as authorities scrambled to stem the selling.
Wall Street's volatility "fear gauge" ‌soared, the Nasdaq sank 5.5% and $3 trillion was wiped off S&P 500 firms, with investors worried Democrats, who dominated midterm elections this week, will apply brakes to the AI boom.
"It's actually a bit of a disaster," said Christopher Forbes, head of Asia and Middle ​East at CMC Markets.
"(Clients) were long index, long stocks, and they all got carried out," he said. "All night, all day – we had client margin calls, client complaints ... because it's a very emotional thing, right? People are wedded to their positions and views on a stock or outcome and you're telling them, look, you've just lost money."
The political jitters are hitting an AI trade already on shaky footing due to worry about return on massive spending in AI-related infrastructure, with the meltdown spurring margin calls and spooking retail investors and hedge funds alike.
"The selloff shows that AI stock prices had been built on rosy illusions about the future, and now that illusion is gone," said ‌Dong Baozhen, chairman of asset manager Lingtong Shengtai.
"The US stock market has ⁠been the standard-bearer and backbone of the global AI bull run. Now that backbone has snapped. Can AI bull markets elsewhere hold up on their own?"
By the Asian afternoon, stocks cut some losses as authorities worked to soothe nerves, with South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il temporarily easing rules on retail investors' ⁠leveraged investments.
Multiple people told Reuters the Ministry of Finance in Taiwan called senior executives at state-owned banks in the morning and instructed them to support the market.
Taiwan stocks closed down 4.5%, recovering somewhat from their early morning slump. For the week, the index clocked a 12.2% decline, its biggest since 1991, LSEG data showed.
Nasdaq futures were up 0.8% while European stock futures were last down 1%, indicating sentiment remained fragile.
Korean AI chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell nearly ​6% ​and 9.4% respectively, cutting steep losses from earlier. TSMC fell as much 8.5% in Taiwan, before closing down 4.7%.
In Japan, ​Kioxia plunged 11% while AI investor SoftBank Group slid 11%, with the cost of ‌insuring against the Japanese firm defaulting on debt jumped to its highest in four years.
"After damage like the sort we've been facing, it is difficult to think that we simply can bounce from here," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers.
"We may be oversold in the short term, but the underlying questions and causes can't simply be wiped away."
Investor fear also centred on whether a stalling AI infrastructure expansion could hurt smaller firms whose capacity to raise funds has already been limited by higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions.
AI cloud computing provider CoreWeave, which has become a barometer of investor anxiety over heavy AI spending and borrowing, slumped 10%, while its 5-year credit default swap spreads widened to a record level.
The selling indicates investors are starting to factor in increased local opposition to data centres, with analysts saying markets have ‌yet to fully consider the cost such building has imposed on communities.
Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa on Thursday said the state ​will introduce laws to protect residents with regards to data centres, citing their impact on rural communities.
Still, some analysts said the ​selloff was overdone and the bottom was not far off.
"Today we are bound to see further ​liquidation of margin accounts, which suggests we are likely in the final stage of capitulation," said Allen Huang, a vice president of Mega Financial Holding's equities trading department.
"Even ‌TSMC hit its daily limit down circuit breaker at one point, which typically marks ​the tail end of a downturn. When TSMC gets ​sold off, that means all stocks have been thoroughly dumped," Huang said.
Bonds gained in Asia, with US Treasuries as well as government bonds in Japan and China rising. The US dollar lured haven flows as did the Japanese yen and Swiss franc. [FRX/]
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was at 4.838%, hovering near the lowest level since September 9. The ​10-year JGB yield dropped as much as 9 bps to 1.795%, the lowest ‌since June 30. [JP/] [US/]
"Bonds are increasingly behaving like bonds again, with income re-emerging as the primary driver of returns and restoring their traditional diversification benefits," said Masahiko Loo, chief fixed income strategist ​at State Street Investment Management.
"This looks more like a reassessment of AI policy risk than a reassessment of the AI cycle."
(Reporting by Tom Westbrook and Ankur Banerjee in Singapore, Liang-sa ​Loh and Roger Tung in Taipei and Samuel Shen in Shanghai; Editing by Sam Holmes and Christopher Cushing)
items.title: Stocks tumble as AI panic sweeps markets, bonds draw haven demand

Title: What Just Happened To Thomson Reuters Stock?
Author: Trefis Team   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:26 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T04:26:58+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Thomson Reuters (TRI) stock fell 9.9% on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 0.4%. The decline came on the day the company reported third-quarter results. At first glance, the quarter appeared solid: revenue rose 10% from a year earlier, and management said growth and margins came in ahead of its own expectations. So why did the stock fall?
Why Did Thomson Reuters Stock Fall On Third-Quarter Results?
News reports linked the fall to results that missed analysts' estimates for both earnings and revenue. Adjusted earnings per share came to $0.81, against the $0.89 analysts expected, though management said the figure was still up 14% from a year earlier.
Management also guided to a slower fourth quarter. The company expects organic revenue growth of about 8% in the final three months of 2026, after posting 10% in the third quarter, and it sees its news business roughly flat from a year earlier. For the full year, management raised its organic growth outlook to a range of 8.5% to 9%, from about 8% before.
Looking further out, management said that, in its early thinking, it currently expects to spend part of the margin gains it would otherwise get from growth on AI investments during 2027. Management said its current investments are going into products such as Westlaw and CoCounsel.
Did Similar Stocks Fall With Thomson Reuters?
Most did, but by much less: Thomson Reuters fell largely on its own. Within its diversified support services industry group, 12 of 17 other companies worth $2 billion or more declined. Their median move was a fall of just 0.4%, and only one of them dropped 5% or more. The industrials sector fund XLI rose 0.9% the same session.
Thomson Reuters' peers on the Trefis list fell further than its industry group, but still far less than it did. Four of the five stocks dropped, with FactSet Research Systems posting the largest decline at 3.2%. Fair Isaac was unchanged.
Where Thomson Reuters Stock Stands After The Drop
A drop of this scale is rare for the stock. Over the prior 365 days, it had fallen this much or more in just one session. It has also lost 26.1% since October 31, 2025, while the S&P 500 returned 11.9%. Both figures include dividends.
The shares closed at $110.18, well below their 52-week closing high of $158.16 on November 3, 2025. They had bottomed at $76.55 on June 22, 2026, and rallied from there. Even after this drop, the stock is up 17.1% since May 5, 2026, against 4.8% for the S&P 500.
Thomson Reuters is expected to report its fourth-quarter results in February 2027. Organic revenue growth, which management guided at about 8%, is the figure to watch.

Title: Should You Wait Before Buying Bloom Energy Stock?
Author: Trefis Team   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:53 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T04:53:27+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Bloom Energy (BE) said on October 22 that third-quarter revenue rose 138% from a year earlier, and it raised its full-year outlook for the third time in fiscal 2026. The stock closed on November 3 at 38.1% below its highest close of the past year, set in June, although it is still up 61.9% over twelve months. After a fall that size, has Bloom's price come back in line with its business, or is buying still early?
What Does Bloom Energy Stock Cost After The Fall?
The decline leaves Bloom cheaper against its own recent past, but not against the broader market. The stock now costs 16.5 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.2 times for the S&P 500. That multiple sat at 21.3 at the end of September, higher than at 31 of the 33 quarter ends since 2018.
That price accompanies Bloom's best operating margin in years. The margin reached 14.8% over the twelve months to September, the highest at any quarter end since 2017. Revenue more than doubled over those twelve months, and management said product revenue crossed $1 billion in a single quarter for the first time in the third quarter.
Cash fell short of profit in the latest quarter. Bloom posted $250 million in third-quarter net income, but its operations used $27 million. Management attributed the outflow mainly to more inventory, contract assets and receivables.
The stock price appears to assume another revenue jump. The consensus estimate projects $1.5 billion of revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, which ends in December, compared with the $1.24 billion Bloom reported for the third quarter.
Management raised its full-year revenue guidance on October 22 to a range of $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion. The midpoint of that forecast is up from the $4.05 billion the company projected in July. The timing of a small number of deliveries around year end will determine where Bloom lands within that range, management said.
Reaching those targets may carry a cost. Management said Bloom is ramping new production lines and expediting deliveries to meet customer timelines, adding that it thinks this carries some near term cost. So the price appears to assume both the revenue jump and that the cost of delivering it stays contained, while demand for Bloom Energy servers as on-site power keeps growing.
Bloom is expected to report its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results in February 2027. Its stock has risen more often than it has fallen following recent reports. Shares rose in the two trading days after four of its last six reports, by as much as 25.2% after the April 2026 report. The stock fell after the other two, dropping 6.4% following the October 22 report and 3.5% after the July 2025 report.
Bloom has also fallen further than the market during past shocks. The stock lost 38.0% in the 2025 tariff shock, against 19.0% for the S&P 500, a fall about as deep as the one the stock has taken since its June high.
When Bloom reports, the numbers to watch are fourth-quarter revenue against that consensus, and whether cash from operations turns positive again after the third quarter's outflow. If revenue beats that consensus and operating cash turns positive, today's price may start to look earned; if not, buying before the February 2027 report may still be early.

Title: Ben Cowen Says After Nasdaq Fall, Bitcoin Could Head Back to $58,000
Author: Darryn Pollock   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:40 AM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T04:40:10+00:00
=== BODY ===
Crypto analyst Ben Cowen, says the Nasdaq Composite has erased all post-midterm gains. He says a slide to its summer lows could drag Bitcoin (BTC) to $58,000.
That price sits near Bitcoin's June low, the weakest point of 2026, so a retest would erase its entire rebound.
Cowen points to 2018, when the S&P 500 gained 2.1% the day after the midterms. However, three events then drove stocks lower into December, he says.
First, Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Jerome Powell said in October 2018 that rates sat far from the neutral level. CNBC tied that remark to the S&P 500's worst month since 2011.
Meanwhile, Cowen says markets now price two more rate hikes despite the tech selloff.
Second, Caterpillar, 3M, and Ford flagged tariff-linked cost pressure that October, Bloomberg reported.
Therefore, Cowen argues, today's tariffs add to inflation and keep the Fed hawkish.
Third, Cowen says tech stocks reversed in late 2018 as regulators scrutinized large platforms. He argues AI fears now play that role.
On Thursday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed about 1,800 points lower, ABC reported. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq entered correction territory, a drop of 10% or more from its peak.
Cowen then linked the two markets in a follow-up post.
"If the NASDAQ can go back to the summer lows, then so can Bitcoin."
Bitcoin has followed big tech lower before. An earlier Big Tech selloff pulled it toward $62,000 in June.
In contrast, Morgan Stanley strategist Mike Wilson calls any midterm dip a buying chance, an earlier Q4 report noted.
However, the analogy could break if the Fed softens. Powell shifted to a dovish tone in late November 2018.
BlackRock managing director Jeffrey Rosenberg says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh links tighter financial conditions to AI. The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% last week.

Title: Is Carvana Stock Paying You Enough For The Swings?
Author: Trefis Team   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:12 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T04:12:37+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
If you own Carvana (CVNA), the online used-car retailer, or are considering buying the stock after its 31.3% jump in the five sessions to November 4, 2026, the shares likely sit alongside investments that already track the broader market. A stock that moves this hard changes how far your entire portfolio rises and falls each day. So has the stock earned enough to make those swings worth holding?
Carvana Paid Less Per Swing Than The S&P 500
No, not over the past five years. In the five years to November 4, 2026, Carvana stock returned 5.4% a year, compared with 11.9% a year for the S&P 500. Its annual volatility over those years, which measures how widely a stock's price swings in a typical year, was 112.4%, compared with 17.0% for the index.
When dividing each return by its volatility, Carvana stock earned 0.048 points of yearly return for each point of swing, compared with 0.7 for the S&P 500. The index therefore paid its holders far more than Carvana did for every bit of movement they experienced.
How Far Does Carvana Move With The S&P 500?
On the average day the S&P 500 rose in the year to November 4, 2026, Carvana climbed about 2.4 times as far, gaining $156 on a $10,000 holding. On the average day the index fell, Carvana again dropped more than twice as far, and the same holding lost $142.
Carvana's beta, which tracks how far the stock moves for each 1% move in the index, was 2.15 over that year. Its volatility for the year was 61.7%, compared with 12.9% for the S&P 500. Carvana therefore adds to the market risk you already carry rather than steadying it. Some of its moves are its own, however. Its daily moves lined up with the index's only loosely, showing a correlation of 0.45, where 1 means the two always move together.
The stock may continue to move this much while Carvana is still chasing a goal far beyond what it sells today. Management said on the October 28, 2026 call that the company is building toward 3 million units a year, compared with a run rate of 870,000 now. Revenue grew 42.4% from a year earlier to $8.04 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Management says growth is limited mainly by how fast the company can scale its supply chain, and it is still investing in its reconditioning centers to raise production.
Carvana's profits are also recent. The company posted an operating loss in the twelve months to September 30, 2023, and an 8.7% operating margin in the twelve months to September 30, 2026. A company still this far from its own goal is a bet still being proven.
If Carvana moves as it did over the past year, the money you hold in it will on average rise more than twice as far as the index on an up day and fall more than twice as far on a down day, though any single day can still go the other way. If you already own other car retailers, Carvana's daily moves over the past year tracked theirs less closely than they tracked the S&P 500, with correlations of 0.23 to 0.38 against 0.45. Carvana is expected to report its next results in February 2027. Retail units sold, the measure of its progress toward that 3 million goal, is the number to watch.

Title: Was Nutanix's Rise Driven By The Company Or Its Industry?
Author: Trefis Team   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:48 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T04:48:21+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Over the past five years, a single stock outperformed 61 of the 69 other companies in its industry. That stock belongs to Nutanix (NTNX), a hybrid cloud software provider operating in the Systems Software space. Before you read on, take a guess: did the industry lift Nutanix, or did Nutanix pull away from its industry on its own?
How Far Nutanix Is Ahead Of Its Industry
Shares of Nutanix advanced 78.3% over the five years through November 3, 2026. Over that same period, the typical company in the Systems Software industry lost 54.1%.
Systems Software industry (median company)
Information Technology sector (median company)
Most systems software stocks lost money for their investors over those five years, whereas Nutanix delivered gains. Among the larger companies in the space, CrowdStrike and Zeta Global performed even better.
The broader market provided some help. The S&P 500 advanced 62.4% over the same five years, although the largest companies dominate that index, and the typical stock across the market fell 4.7%. Nutanix still finished ahead of the index.
The company received no such support from its sector or industry. The typical Information Technology company fell 24.9% over five years, and within that sector, Systems Software ranked 11th of 12 industries. Nutanix rose against its industry's tide, not with it.
Nutanix expanded at a slightly faster pace than its peers. The company posted average annual revenue growth of 15.3% over the last three years, compared with 13.6% for the typical systems software company.
A more significant change occurred over the five-year window. Nutanix more than doubled its revenue between fiscal 2021 and fiscal 2026, and over the same years, its operating margin shifted from a loss of 47.5% of revenue to a profit of 9.6%. Its diluted share count also rose 37.7%, so revenue per share grew about 49%.
Investors paid only slightly more for each unit of sales. Nutanix traded at 5.8 times sales on June 30, 2021, and reached 6.1 times at the November 3, 2026 close. Five years to the day after the 2021 figure, on June 30, 2026, it traded at 4.8 times. The business itself, rather than a higher multiple, made the difference.
Nutanix reports two lines of business: product, and support, entitlements and other services. The product segment accounted for 52.9% of revenue in fiscal 2025, following a 25.6% increase that year. During the latest call, management pointed to support for external storage, noting the offering brought several large wins in fiscal Q4 2026, including a new customer among the Global 2000.
Is Nutanix Still Ahead Over The Past Year?
Over the past year, Nutanix outperformed 54.7% of its industry peers, compared with 88.4% over the five-year period. The company remains ahead of most competitors, but the lead has narrowed. Over that year, Nutanix shares fell 9.1%, while the S&P 500 rose 10.5%.
During its August 26, 2026 call, management guided to an adjusted operating margin of 24% to 25% for fiscal 2027, up from an adjusted 22.5% in fiscal 2026. That guide is a forecast, and management said it reflects the expected operating impact of a restructuring that affected about 5% of the workforce. Management also assumed that server supply constraints will continue.
Nutanix's operating margin is the figure to watch when the company next reports, expected in December 2026.
Not necessarily on Nutanix alone, if your goal is long-term wealth. Wealth is built by owning the companies that keep outperforming, the leaders of their industries, wherever they are. Nutanix is one. Over the five years to November 2026, its stock rose 78.3%, ahead of 61 of the 69 other companies in Systems Software, where the typical company fell 54.1%.

Title: Do You Like Cash? Consider Reddit Stock
Author: Trefis Team   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:05 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T04:05:07+00:00
=== BODY ===
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Reddit (RDDT) offers investors more cash for its price than most large companies. Its free cash flow yield sits at 6.1%, compared with 4.1% for the median S&P 500 company. That valuation follows a hard year, as Reddit stock fell 45.7% in the twelve months to November 4 while the S&P 500 returned 14.9%. Cheap cash means either a bargain or a business investors expect to shrink. So which is it for Reddit?
Reddit's Sales And Cash Are Still Growing Fast
So far, Reddit's figures lean to the bargain side. Revenue rose 62.2% over the twelve months to September from the twelve months before, and free cash flow reached $1.2 billion, up from $510 million a year earlier.
Shareholders own a piece of the free cash Reddit produces whether or not it is paid out, just as they own a share of its profit. When investors start to value that cash, the share price tends to rise, more so when the cash is growing.
The company also owes almost nothing. Reddit ended September with $31.4 million of debt against $3.03 billion of cash and short-term investments, leaving lenders with little claim on what the business makes.
Reddit Warns Daily Users Could Fall In Q4
The risk Reddit named on its October 29 call centers on users, not cash. Management said search referral traffic fell meaningfully in the third quarter and dropped by an average of more than 1 million referrals a week in October. If that pace continues, management said daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from 130 million.
The share price appears to assume fewer users will cost Reddit revenue, but so far the drop in daily users remains a forecast rather than a result. Management did say total sessions are down because of the decline in search referral traffic, and the stock fell 29% on October 30, the day after that call. News reports that day also blamed a revenue outlook that came in below Wall Street's expectations. Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion. That would be 38% to 42% more than a year earlier, slower than the 53% growth Reddit reported for the third quarter, but still growth.
Management is working to move users onto the app. Reddit shifted part of its U.S. marketing from the web into app installs, and in the fourth quarter it begins testing a logged-in only Reddit in select markets outside the U.S. Management said 80% of what Reddit earns from its users comes from people on its app or logged in.
Management said Google is not sending people to Reddit the way it used to. For an owner, the open question is whether Reddit's cash keeps growing as that goes on. The company's cash record runs through September, and the fall in daily users that management warned about would come after it, in the fourth quarter. Debt is not an open question, since Reddit holds far more cash than it owes.
Daily users, and fourth-quarter revenue against management's guide, are the measures to watch when Reddit next reports, expected in February 2027.

Title: S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow Futures Dip As Investors Step Back From AI And Tech With Nasdaq In Correction Territory —  NVDA, AAPL, UBER, SOXX In Focus
Author: Shashank Nayar   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:00 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T01:00:30+00:00
=== BODY ===
The S&P 500 ended Thursday 4.4% lower, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 3.4%.
Apple Inc. raised $7.5 billion from its high-grade bond offering.
iShares Semiconductor ETF was down more than 12% for its worst day since March 2020, when COVID struck.
U.S. stock indices ended lower on Thursday, with futures extending declines after hours as investors heavily sold off tech and chipmaker stocks amid concerns a Democratic win could derail the pace of data center and AI buildout, delaying capex recovery.
The S&P 500 ended Thursday 4.4% lower, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, well in correction territory, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 3.4%. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, lost 4.5%.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
S&P 500 futures lost 0.8%, while Nasdaq-100 futures slid 1.3%. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 264 points, or 0.5%.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 4.5%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) dropped 3.5%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) ended 6.5% lower on Thursday.
Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped between 11% and 12% each on Thursday amid weakness in Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Tech (MU),Broadcom (AVGO) and memory chip maker SanDisk (SNDK). The broader Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) dropped 5.8%.
Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for SPY, QQQ, and DIA was 'bearish.'
The sudden acceleration in the tech selloff was heavily catalyzed by the outcome of Tuesday's midterm elections, which saw Democrats capture majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Electoral campaigns increasingly centered around public pushback against massive data center developments, driven by community anxieties over escalating electricity costs, environmental strains, and grid reliability.
In Texas, newly elected Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa amplified these regional concerns by advocating for an immediate moratorium on new data center construction. Because data centers serve as the physical backbone for AI infrastructure—packed densely with rows of advanced semiconductors—any regulatory roadblock or deceleration in data center spending threatens to translate into severe long-term headwinds for chipmakers.
Investors are "stepping away until they get a better sense of the implications of the midterms around the AI capex cycle in particular, which is the biggest economic tailwind we've had going for us for the last, call it, three years," Tim Holland, chief investment officer at Orion, told CNBC. "It's about tone and tenor from the party that did really well, incredibly well, at the federal level and at the state level."
Moreover, Big Short fame Michael Burry sold 25% of his put positions in the $58 billion VanEck Semiconductor ETF amid the deep sellout seen in tech shares. "The SMH put positions even after the sale, however, have become very large positions," he wrote.
Nvidia is pursuing a plan to turn existing telecom facilities into small AI data centers as a way to deploy its chips more quickly and sidestep growing local resistance to new construction, The Information reported on Thursday.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) is set to raise about $7.5 billion from a high-grade bond offering, Bloomberg reported.
Shares of DoorDash (DASH) slumped 10% on Thursday after rivals Amazon (AMZN) and Uber Technologies (UBER) struck a partnership giving Amazon Prime members free delivery on Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more when placed directly through Amazon's website or app.
Yucca Growth Infrastructure LLC, the firm building power infrastructure for Oracle Corp.'s (ORCL) New Mexico data center, has reportedly agreed to waive a looming regulatory deadline, instead of risking an application denial.
Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) opted not to extend a major data center agreement with Nvidia-backed AI startup Nscale.

Title: Nasdaq futures rise, Dow sinks after AI rout slams Wall St; payrolls in focus
Author: Ambar Warrick   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:38 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T01:38:07+00:00
=== BODY ===
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures were a mixed bag early-Friday, with Nasdaq futures heralding some recovery after a bruising selldown in tech and artificial intelligence this week.
Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »
Dow futures fell as focus turned to upcoming labor market data for more cues on the economy and interest rates, with markets on guard over any signs of outsized labor market strength.
Nasdaq 100 Futures rose 0.68% to 26,936.0 points by 01:17 ET (06:17 GMT). S&P 500 Futures fell 0.1% to 7,375.50 points, while Dow Jones Futures fell 1% to 51,082.0 points.
Futures remained skittish after Wall Street suffered its worst day in nearly 19 months on Thursday, battered chiefly by a major wipeout in high-flying technology and artificial intelligence stocks.
Chipmakers were by far the worst hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sliding 12.25% for the day. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA), which recently relinquished its title as the world's most valuable listed company, slumped nearly 10% on Thursday, while rival AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) slid 17%.
Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT), Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META), Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN), and Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL)– all of which are heavily exposed to data center spending– fell between 2% and 4%, while iPhone maker Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) performed relatively better with a 1.5% drop.
Losses spilled over into Friday's Asian session, with South Korea's KOSPI on the verge of a 20% wipeout from late-October levels, while Japan's Nikkei 225 entered a bear market.
The Democratic Party's sweep of the midterm elections– where it secured majorities in both chambers of Congress– sparked heightened concerns over more regulatory scrutiny towards AI development and data center construction.
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »
Texas Governor-Elect, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, called for a pause on any new data center construction until there were laws to protect citizens in place.
Her comments reflected a broader rhetoric among Democratic lawmakers, especially amid growing voter pushback against more data center construction across the country.
The development came amid already growing doubts over the long-term feasibility of AI, after a host of middling September quarter earnings from Wall Street's biggest firms pointed to uncertain returns on their massive AI investments.
Separately, reports said AI major Anthropic was facing increased investor scrutiny over its plans to publicly list later this month, with Reuters reporting that the startup could potentially delay a listing.
The NASDAQ Composite slumped 5.5% on Thursday, the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 3.4%. The Dow took some support from flows into non-tech, defensive sectors like utilities and consumer staples.
Beyond the AI rout, focus on Friday will be squarely on key labor data that is likely to factor into the Federal Reserve's plans for interest rates.
Nonfarm payrolls data for September is due Friday morning, and is expected to show a pickup in jobs growth from the prior month.
Any signs of resilience in the labor market give the Fed more headroom to hike interest rates– a scenario that could herald more pain for Wall Street.
The Fed raised rates by 25 basis points in September, with policymakers indicating that sticky inflation was likely to elicit more hikes.

Title: Why did Apple Stock Hit an All-Time High Amid US Stock Market Crash?
Author: Jakub Dziadkowiec   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:50 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T01:50:26+00:00
=== BODY ===
Apple (AAPL) stock hit a record $354.50 on November 4, then slipped about 1.5% Thursday while the Nasdaq fell 5.52%.
Shares closed at $349.51 Wednesday, up 5.31%, as investors rotated from AI hardware into Apple's lighter AI spending. Thursday tested that safe-haven trade.
The move came after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections. Investors read the result as gridlock, sending the Dow up more than 3%.
Meanwhile, capital rotated out of AI hardware names on fears of new data center limits. Nvidia fell about 3% that day, while Apple's lighter AI spending made it a tech safe haven.
That shift could also ease pressure on memory chip prices, Apple's main cost headwind this year. Falling oil prices and Treasury yields added further support.
As a result, Apple's market value climbed to $5.08 trillion. That made it the world's most valuable company again, overtaking Nvidia at $4.83 trillion.
Stocks plummeted Thursday as investors accelerated their exit from tech on fears of a slower data center buildout, CNBC reported. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, the S&P 500 lost 4.36%, and the Dow dropped 3.44%.
Apple fell about 1.5% to around $344, according to TradingView. Nvidia fell 9% and Broadcom 10%.
The Magnificent Seven tech stocks lost close to $900 billion in value heading into the final hour. Nvidia alone shed about $374 billion, while Apple shed nearly $59 billion.
Apple still fell, so its safe haven status holds only in relative terms. The stock remains up about 26% year to date.
The rally erased losses that followed Apple's fiscal fourth-quarter report on November 2. Revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $114.5 billion, according to the company's release. Earnings per share of $2.10 beat the $1.99 consensus.
However, Apple guided December-quarter gross margin to 45% to 46%, down from 47.9%. Executives flagged rising memory costs, and shares fell for two straight sessions.
On the daily chart, shares pulled back 7.5% from the October 23 high of $351.73 to $325.33 on November 3.
That decline reached the 0.382 Fibonacci retracement level near $325. The zone held as support for the second time, after a similar test in early October.
Shares briefly lost the 50-day moving average (MA) at $335 during the dip. However, the next session reclaimed it with a strong bullish candle.
Volume reached 89.6 million shares, the highest since late June, suggesting strong buyer participation. Meanwhile, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) climbed to 58, returning to bullish territory.
A daily close above $354.50 would put Apple in price discovery, with no historical resistance overhead. However, the upper wick on Wednesday's candle hinted at profit-taking near the record, and shares slipped on Thursday.
On the downside, $340 is first support, and Thursday's decline held above it. The 50-day MA at $335 comes next, and a break below $325 could expose the 0.618 Fibonacci level at $305.
Valuation remains a risk, with Apple trading near 36 times forward earnings. Further tech selling is the larger threat to the setup.

Title: The Nasdaq Composite Just Shattered Its Single-Session Point-Loss Record: 3 Reasons These Elevator-Down Moves May Be Just Beginning
Author: Sean Williams, The Motley Fool   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:10 AM GMT+1 7 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T01:10:02+00:00
=== BODY ===
To say it was a rough day for Wall Street's major stock indexes would be an understatement. The timeless Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) shed 1,833 points, the benchmark S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) lost 335 points, and the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) plummeted 1,422 points on Nov. 5.
While the Nasdaq Composite's 5.52% decline didn't crack the 20 largest percentage drops on record, its 1,422-point single-session loss shattered its previous record tumble of 1,122 points, set on June 5, 2026.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
The uncomfortable reality for investors is that there are three reasons these elevator-down moves may be just beginning.
Prediction markets widely forecast that Democrats would sweep Congress on Election Night, and that's exactly what happened. By early January, President Donald Trump will be working with a Democrat-led Congress.
Trump has repeatedly stated that he'll use his presidential veto power to effectively maintain the status quo. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite initially rallied on Nov. 4 with the understanding that the president could veto stricter AI regulation bills sent to his desk from a Democrat-controlled Congress.
But what investors overlooked was a "blue wave" at the gubernatorial level. Democratic governors flipped five former Republican seats (two state elections have yet to be called by the Associated Press). Three of these flipped seats (Texas, Georgia, and Ohio) are focal points for data center planning and construction.
Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas has pledged to ban data center approvals until her state's legislature passes laws on electricity, water, air, and property rights. Most Democratic lawmakers favor limiting data center expansion and stricter testing/vetting on large language models.
In other words, stricter AI regulation at the state level can circumvent Trump's veto power.
This could be particularly damaging to AI hardware companies that have enjoyed never-before-seen pricing power. In addition to insatiable enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, persistent supply shortages have lifted the pricing power of AI hardware providers. If data center approval moratoriums result in a more balanced supply-vs-demand outlook for hardware, the pricing power and gross margin of leading AI stocks may crater.
Secondly, the bond market has, for months, been sending an unmistakable warning to equity markets that the AI infrastructure build-out was in trouble.
When public companies issue debt, it's typically priced at a par value of $1,000, which is quoted as $1 on financial websites. Given that bond prices and yields are inversely related, yields go up if a bond trades below its par value.
The reasons bond prices might decline include skepticism about the long-term solvency of the underlying company or bond traders' desire to receive a higher yield given the implied risk factors.
Several foundational companies tied to the AI infrastructure build-out have seen their bond prices collapse. Space Exploration Technologies' (NASDAQ:SPCX) recently issued 2056 notes are trading at $0.83 on the dollar; Nvidia's (NASDAQ:NVDA) 2060 notes are clocking in at $0.63 on the dollar; and CoreWeave's (NASDAQ:CRWV) 2031 notes (issued this year) are trading at $0.78 on the dollar.
These discounts to par value denote mounting skepticism regarding the sustainability of the AI data center build-out.
The stock market also entered 2026 at its second-priciest valuation in history, according to the S&P 500's Shiller Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio, also known as the Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE Ratio).
Whereas the time-tested P/E ratio is arrived at using trailing 12-month earnings, the Shiller P/E Ratio is based on average inflation-adjusted earnings over the trailing decade. When recessions arise and corporate earnings turn negative, the Shiller P/E Ratio remains useful, which isn't always the case for the traditional P/E ratio.
When backtested to January 1871, the CAPE Ratio has surpassed 30 on six occasions, including the present. Following each of the previous five instances, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and/or Nasdaq Composite eventually (keyword!) plunged between 20% and 89%.
Although the Shiller P/E Ratio offers no help in deciphering precisely when the stock market will reverse course or which catalyst will push it over the edge, 156 years of history conclusively show that premium valuations aren't sustainable over the long run.
While AI growth rates have been off the charts, every next-big-thing investment trend for more than 30 years has eventually endured a bubble-bursting event early in its expansion. Historical precedent suggests it's not a matter of if but of when the AI bubble bursts.

Author: Roushni Nair   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:03 AM GMT+1 2 min read

=== BODY ===
Investing.com -- U.S. President Donald Trump blamed Democrats for Wall Street's sharp selloff following their sweeping midterm election victories, saying the stock market had suffered one of its worst days in history and warning that Americans' 401(k) retirement accounts had taken a hit.
Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »
Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and Senate in Tuesday's November 3 elections, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major setback for Republicans.
The results also included Democratic victories in key gubernatorial races and widespread support for local measures restricting data-centre developments.
Wall Street initially welcomed the outcome. On Wednesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,569 points, or 3%, while the S&P 500 gained 1.6% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.4%, as investors anticipated reduced political uncertainty.
However, that rally reversed sharply on Thursday as investors reassessed the implications of Democratic victories for the artificial intelligence industry.
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »
The S&P 500 dropped 4.4% to 7,353.73, its steepest decline since the April 2025 tariff selloff. The Dow lost 1,833 points, or 3.4%, while the Nasdaq plunged 5.5%, its worst session in 18 months. The Russell 2000 also fell 4.4%.
The losses were concentrated in technology and semiconductor stocks amid concerns that Democratic lawmakers and newly elected governors could introduce tighter restrictions on data-centre construction, potentially slowing the expansion of AI infrastructure.
At least 38 jurisdictions passed restrictions or bans on data-centre projects, while Texas' incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa has advocated a moratorium on new developments.
Nvidia fell around 9%, Advanced Micro Devices dropped 17% and Micron declined more than 17%.
The Nasdaq's market capitalisation shed about $2 trillion during Thursday's selloff, according to Reuters, as investors reassessed the growth outlook for AI infrastructure.
While the Dow's decline marked its worst second trading session following a midterm election in records dating back to 1896, Thursday's broader market losses were not unprecedented. The S&P 500's 4.4% decline was its largest since April 2025.

Title: Beijing seeks to bolster AI shares
Author: Julien Girault, with Luna Lin in Beijing   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 8:17 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T07:17:56+00:00
=== BODY ===
After recent sharp drops for some Chinese tech stocks, Beijing is trying to prop them up -- seeing the sector, and in particular AI, as a central strategic priority.
In August, buzzy Chinese startup Unitree, whose walking, dancing humanoids are often used by AI researchers trying to make robots act autonomously, went public.
Its shares skyrocketed on its Shanghai debut in August -- but almost three months later they are down 40 percent from their peak that day.
Chinese chipmakers Moore Threads and MetaX -- touted as challengers to US behemoth Nvidia -- have both plunged by around 50 percent over the past six months.
Similar steep falls can be seen across Shanghai's tech-focused Star50 index, China's answer to Wall Street's Nasdaq, which is down only around six percent over the same period.
Volatility on Wall Street hasn't helped -- the Nasdaq plunged 5.5 percent on Thursday -- with fears that the vast sums spent on AI infrastructure will not translate into big profits.
However, the Chinese government is taking steps.
Officials this week reactivated liquidity-injection tools aimed at encouraging share purchases while boosting the trading volume of state-backed investment funds, according to local media reports.
On Tuesday, net capital inflows into nine exchange-traded funds (ETFs), commonly used by Beijing to prop up the market, reached 120 billion yuan ($18 billion) -- a near-record, according to Bloomberg data, targeting tech stocks in particular.
The Financial Times also reported this week that Chinese regulators had told banks to halt company listings in an attempt to boost market liquidity.
"Chinese technology shares have been under significant pressure, with investors concerned about weak domestic demand, intense competition and disappointing earnings," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets.
However, now "fresh policy support, lower valuations and hopes of improving sentiment are encouraging investors to revisit a sector that has struggled for much of the year", she added.
Overall, tech investors in China remain optimistic, said Ajin Jin, partner at Shanghai-based investment firm Kunquan.
"In both Beijing and Shanghai, weekly roadshows are still taking place, and every single one is packed to the rafters, with people even sitting in the aisles," he said.
Li Daxiao, one of China's most prominent investment gurus, also said "the burgeoning development of the industry is unstoppable" and should be clearly distinguished from "share price fluctuations".
"Technology shares have been affected by external risks and have fallen in tandem with their counterparts in the US, Japan and South Korea," he told AFP.
Stephen Inness of SPI Asset Management said that "a state-backed effort would add to steps taken by China last month to stabilise its equity market".
However, he warned the measures "have so far proved insufficient against the backdrop of a weak domestic economy and doubts over AI earnings".
items.title: Beijing seeks to bolster AI shares

At the short end of the curve, the policy-sensitive two-year JGB yield tumbled to 1.731%, hitting its lowest mark since September and similarly logging its largest one-day drop since July.
The dramatic rush into Japanese sovereign paper followed a brutal session on Wall Street overnight, where equity benchmarks suffered their deepest losses in over a year and a half.

The scale of the equity drawdown echoed the volatility of the April 2025 tariff shock, instantly extinguishing the risk-on enthusiasm that had propelled global bourses earlier in the week and triggering an immediate rotation into low-beta government bonds across Asia.
The catalyst behind the Wall Street rout was a sudden, dark reassessment of the artificial intelligence boom following Tuesday's decisive Democratic sweep of the U.S. Congress.
Chipmakers and infrastructure providers bore the brunt of the liquidation after investors recognized that an opposition-controlled House and Senate significantly increases the odds of aggressive federal antitrust enforcement and tougher environmental oversight.
Market anxiety was heightened by key Democratic election wins across several battleground states where local opposition to power-hungry, water-intensive data centers has mounted rapidly over the past year.
The ensuing liquidity shock spilled directly into Tokyo trading rooms on Friday morning, completely overturning the domestic monetary narrative.
Only 24 hours earlier, Japanese yields had been anchored by hawkish minutes from the Bank of Japan's September meeting, which had reinforced market wagers that policymakers would lift the nation's benchmark policy rate above its current 31-year high of 1.25% in the coming months.

Title: Nasdaq Stock Market Correction: 3 Words From Warren Buffett To Remember RIght Now
Author: Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 7:27 AM GMT+1 4 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T06:27:02+00:00
=== BODY ===
The Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5% on Thursday, closing in correction territory, defined as a decline of 10% or more from a recent closing high.
Fears of a crackdown on data centers sent tech stocks spiraling after Texas elected a new governor, Gina Hinojosa, who had promised a temporary moratorium on data centers until new rules can be applied to them to ensure that they are not extractive.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
A full-on backlash against data centers seems unlikely, and there's always the possibility that they could move to neighboring states or even outside the country. AI demand is strong enough that new capacity will be created somewhere.
Thursday's crash was also a gut check for investors, and a reminder that sentiment can change quickly. AI stocks have skyrocketed this year, after all, and a number of them have doubled or better, even after Thursday's retreat. Much of those gains were driven by sentiment, so they are easily given back once that reverses.
For investors looking for some counsel at a time like this, the words of Warren Buffett are always a good source and a reminder to take a long-term view. In fact, not long ago, Buffett offered three words of advice that seem appropriate now.
Market corrections happen on average about every 18 months. In other words, they are a normal part of the investment cycle, and investors should be prepared for them.
Back in March, after the U.S. had launched the war in Iran, the S&P 500 was approaching a correction, and longtime Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett was asked about it on CNBC. "Three times since I've taken over Berkshire, it's gone down more than 50%," he replied. "This is nothing."
Buffett was sitting on a pile of cash at the time, as Berkshire still is, and his comment implied that the sell-off wasn't enough to start deploying that capital.
Buffett's words turned out to be prescient as the market soon bounced back, ripping higher and, in less than a month, was back at all-time highs.
Buffett's advice is a reminder that while it may be painful to lose 5% of your portfolio in a single session, it's not a reason to panic. A 5% pullback in a single day is severe, but pullbacks are a normal part of investing, and making emotional decisions is the wrong move.
The stock market is also unpredictable in the short term, and Buffett's comment preceding a huge rally is a reminder that stocks could bounce off of Thursday's sell-off in the coming days or weeks.
There's another Warren Buffett expression that seems appropriate at the moment as well. Buffett famously counseled: "Be greedy when others are fearful, and fearful when others are greedy.
Thursday's sell-off looks like a lot of fear driven by the data center issue, which comes on the heels of concerns about high interest rates and large capital expenditures, which had also driven the sector lower.
It's worth remembering that despite concerns about a bubble, the tech stocks at the center of the AI boom continue to deliver strong results on the top and bottom lines, and valuations still look very reasonable. Nvidia now trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of less than 23, and Meta Platforms trades at a P/E of just 20.
These stocks look oversold and undervalued, and there are others like them. The current pullback might not be a steep enough sell-off to intrigue Buffett, but those are great prices to pay for high-quality stocks. Investors should keep their focus on the long term and take advantage of dips on top stocks.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $2,601,484 today.*
Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast.
*Stock Advisor returns as of November 6, 2026.
Jeremy Bowman has positions in Nvidia. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Berkshire Hathaway and Nvidia. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

=== META ===
Title: Analysts and investors react to AI market rout
Author: Reuters   Fri, November 6, 2026 at 7:43 AM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-06T06:43:10+00:00
=== BODY ===
Nov 6 (Reuters) - Stock markets were tumbling as fear gripped investors that the Democratic sweep at the midterm elections would lead to regulation and a slowdown of the AI boom that has been propelling computer supply chain stocks all over the world.
The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday in the biggest drop since the tariff-triggered "Liberation Day" rout in 2025.
On Friday in Asia, South Korea's KOSPI slumped 6% and Taiwan's benchmark slid 4.5% ‌to notch its largest weekly fall for more than two decades. [MKTS/GLOB]
Here's what market participants are saying:
CHRISTOPHER FORBES, HEAD OF ASIA AND MIDDLE EAST, CMC MARKETS, SINGAPORE:
"(Clients) were long index, long stocks, and ‌they all got carried out.
"All night, all day – we had client margin calls, client complaints, ... because it's a very emotional thing, right? People are wedded to their positions and views on a stock or outcome and you're telling them, look, you've just lost money.
"And it's not just a slap in terms of valuation. ​It's basically a whole policy and six-year structural shift that says we're now going to pause, we're now going to cool AI, we're now going to cool data centres, approvals and equity capital markets."
DONG BAOZHEN, CHAIRMAN, LINGTONG SHENGTAI, BEIJING:
"The selloff shows that AI stock prices had been built on rosy illusions about the future, and now that illusion is gone," Dong said.
"The US stock market has been the standard-bearer and backbone of the global AI bull run. Now that backbone has snapped. Can AI bull markets elsewhere hold up on their own?"
JASON LUI, HEAD OF APAC EQUITY DERIVATIVES STRATEGY, BNP PARIBAS, HONG KONG:
"We are actually receiving more inquiries about looking at China onshore, because what we have noticed is that over the past month or so, the Chinese policymakers have stepped up on their stabilisation measures.
"Clients tend to ‌view the China onshore trade as a potential diversifier from their global portfolio that tends ⁠to be more driven by US AI."
ALLEN HUANG, VICE PRESIDENT, MEGA FINANCIAL HOLDING EQUITIES TRADING DEPARTMENT:
"Today we are bound to see further liquidation of margin accounts, which suggests we are likely in the final stage of capitulation.
"Even TSMC hit its daily limit-down circuit breaker at one point, which typically marks the tail end of a downturn. When TSMC gets sold off, that means all stocks have been ⁠thoroughly dumped."
STEVE SOSNICK, CHIEF STRATEGIST, INTERACTIVE BROKERS, NEW YORK:
"Investors had already begun to question whether all the copious AI spending would reap sufficient returns to justify billions in debt and equity capital.
"When a group of stocks is heavily owned, priced to perfection, and critical to the bull market's thesis, there is not much room for error if their fundamentals appear threatened.
"After damage like the sort we've been facing, it is difficult to think that we simply can bounce from here. We may be oversold in the short term, but the underlying questions and causes can't simply be ​wiped ​away."
SHANE OLIVER, CHIEF ECONOMIST AND HEAD OF INVESTMENT STRATEGY, AMP, SYDNEY:
"Investors are trying to grapple with what the Democrat win might mean and they ​don't fully know yet. It attests to the broader concern that tech and AI-related trades were ‌trading on relatively high multiples and that left them vulnerable. That concern had been building for a while now, and you could argue that the midterms provided the trigger for a pullback.
"It's too early to say the markets have bottomed, but providing the economic outlook is unaffected, it's probably going to be more of a correction than a bear market."
GEORGE BOUBOURAS, HEAD OF RESEARCH, K2 ASSET MANAGEMENT, MELBOURNE:
"The AI and tech selloff, which began a few months ago on both valuation metrics and impact to free cash flow, has now accelerated on the prospect that the US data centre rollout will be impacted by the change in the Senate and House following the midterms.
"The significant data centre rollout is now anticipated to be scaled back. The unknowns will continue to create uncertainty for markets."
CHARU CHANANA, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, SAXO, SINGAPORE:
"I would caution against interpreting this as the Democrats putting an end to the AI boom. AI leadership remains a strategic priority for both parties, particularly in the competition with China. But there is a difference ‌between supporting AI leadership and allowing the infrastructure buildout to proceed at any cost or pace.
"There is also clearly an element of panic in ​the selling, and positioning is making the adjustment much more violent. When investors begin unwinding these positions simultaneously, the selling can become self-reinforcing, particularly if leverage ​and forced liquidations are involved."
MICHAEL MCCARTHY, CEO, MOOMOO AUSTRALIA AND NZ, SYDNEY:
"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift in ​sentiment.
"Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that shows up in the market by huge swings in either direction. And that's what we appear to have — and last night's emphatic sell-down ‌suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in.
"It's quite possible this could be a ​significant turning point for the US market ... I think a lot ​of the bigger players in the US have declared, in last night's action, that the music has stopped. It's game over."
MARK FUCHS, CIO, FUCHS CAPITAL PARTNERS, SINGAPORE:
"The Democrats had come in with a more circumspect view on data centres and AI ... so there's the broad picture which is probably a little bit of a spending reduction, by virtue of higher bars on data centres generally.
"Asia tech, broadly, is getting further repriced downward on expectations that the demand would be ​somewhat more constrained ... as well as markets pricing cost of capital higher since the Fed ‌started raising rates in September.
"The more important thing, if you take the newer factor of Democrat data centre constraint off the table, (is) the reality is that this sector had been repricing downward for well over a ​month.
"We are preferring more non-AI-related sectors and countries that offer higher nominal GDP and durable domestic growth stories like domestic India, while hedging the currency and index."
(Reporting by Rae Wee, Ankur Banerjee and Gregor Stuart Hunter ​in Singapore and Roger Tung in Taipei and Reuters Shanghai newsroom; Compiled by Tom Westbrook; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus and Jacqueline Wong)

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (ZGGG) on 8 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (ZGGG) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (ZGGG) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=ZGGG&format=raw&date=2026-11-08T19:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (LEMD) on 8 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (LEMD) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (LEMD) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=LEMD&format=raw&date=2026-11-09T02:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM) on 6 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (EHAM) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=EHAM&format=raw&date=2026-11-07T02:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
The 2026 midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the US State gubernatorial race which has the smallest margin of victory. 

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For elections that include runoffs, ranked-choice, or other multi-round elections, the relevant margin of victory will be that of the round in which the winner is determined. 

If two state margins of victory are identical, this market will resolve to the tied state whose name comes first alphabetically.

This market will consider all regular and special gubernatorial elections that are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026. 

For the purposes of this market, US State is defined to exclude territories, the District of Columbia, and any other subdivision that is not a state. 

The resolution source for this market will be a compilation of all of the relevant state election authorities responsible for certifying statewide elections, however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a kinetic strike is conducted on, or forceful seizure of control is taken of, a commercial ship within the defined area on the specified date, between 12:00 AM and 11:59 PM UTC. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The defined area consists of the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Gulf of Oman. An incident occurring outside these three bodies of water will not qualify, including in the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Aden, or the Red Sea.

No attribution is required. A qualifying incident will count regardless of the identity of the party responsible, regardless of whether any state or group claims responsibility, and regardless of whether responsibility is denied, disputed, or never established.

Attacks on military vessels will not be considered.

Missile/drone strikes targeting a ship that are intercepted or otherwise do not directly impact the vessel will not be considered, regardless of damage through debris.

Seize control refers to forcefully boarding and taking control of a commercial ship.

Qualifying incidents include, but are not limited to, drone and missile strikes, aerial bombings, and kinetic actions carried out by operatives in person. Damaged caused by mines will not qualify. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The occurrence, location, and timing of a qualifying incident will be primarily determined based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources. Where multiple sources conflict regarding the occurrence, location, or timing of a relevant incident, this market will remain open until the earlier of: i) the confirmation of the occurrence, location, and timing of the incident based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources or ii) 3 full calendar days (UTC) from the date of the first credibly reported evidence of the incident. If this period would extend past the end date, this market will remain open to allow for 3 full calendar days to pass. If, at the end of the third calendar day, conflicting reports remain as to the occurrence, location, or timing of the incident, the incident will be judged on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

This market will resolve to "Over" if New York Red Bulls and Atlanta United FC combine to score 4 or more goals in this game.

If the combined total is less than 4, this market will resolve to "Under".

If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed. If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve 50–50.

If the game is started but not completed, this market will resolve according to the official final score published on mlssoccer.com. This market refers only to the outcome within the first 90 minutes of regular play plus stoppage time.

However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

The "Team USA" market resolves "Yes" if Team USA finishes with more total points than Team Europe; the "Team Europe" market resolves "Yes" if Team Europe finishes with more total points than Team USA; the "Tie" market resolves "Yes" if the competition ends level on points (e.g., 14–14).

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, these markets remain open until the competition has been completed. If the Ryder Cup is cancelled entirely with no make-up competition, the "Tie" market resolves "Yes" and the "Team USA" and "Team Europe" markets resolve "No".

The primary resolution source will be official information from Ryder Cup Europe / the PGA of America (https://www.rydercup.com); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the third-most valid votes in the first round of this election.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won.
